originality.rationale: Primary full text comparisons identify a distinct arithmetic-dimension phenomenon in three-candidate two-seat optimal Thiele scores. The rational n^(-1/2) rate is already implied by Xia (2025) and is explicitly acknowledged; the unlocated portion is the precise rational leading constant and irrational n^(-1) class with constant 3/pi, not a mere renaming of that known rate. Janeczko–Faliszewski (2023) study tie complexity and empirical rates without this closed asymptotic. No matching published statement was found in the actual literature queries below; this absence is not a uniqueness or exhaustive-priority proof.
residual_risks: General multidimensional lattice scoring-rule theorems, possibly differently named or unpublished, could imply the result as a special case.

value.rationale: Optimal multiwinner ties motivate winner-set semantics and tie breaking. The arithmetic nature of a fixed second-representative weight changes the codimension of tie constraints and therefore the rate at which co-winning committees disappear; the irrational 3/pi coefficient is universal and the rational coefficient depends quantitatively on the reduced numerator and denominator. The phase change and exact constants answer a natural probability-of-ambiguity question, not a routine one-off enumeration. Practical rounded arithmetic is excluded.
